subject: Brightlane — budget owner & procurement intro / next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@brightlanehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Brightlane — follow-up and next steps from discovery

Emily — thanks again for taking the discovery call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

1) What we heard
- Primary use case: improve triage and clinician workflow summaries for post-acute care teams.
- Key success criteria: 15–20% reduction in time-to-document, accuracy on clinical entity extraction comparable to current tool (~95% on core entities), and no PHI leaving Brightlane's VPC for regulated workflows.
- Timeline: pilot decision targeted in Q3 (budget window confirmed by Emily on call).

2) Stakeholders you mentioned (as we noted on the call)
- Technical champion: Emily Zhang (Data Platform) — owns evaluation and integration scope.
- Potential economic buyer / budget owner: (we asked to confirm) — we discussed looping in a VP of Business Ops or Head of Product.
- Procurement / legal: procurement@brightlanehealth.com (to be introduced).

3) Our ask / proposed next steps
- Could you please introduce the economic buyer (name and email) so we can schedule a 30-min alignment call focused on outcomes, licensing model, and ROI?
- Can you loop in procurement/legal for the procurement questionnaire and basic contract terms?
- We'll share a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an ROI template for your finance team to validate impact.

I've attached a short ROI template that our customers find helpful to map savings back to cost centers (Brightlane-ROI-template.xlsx).

Planned internal owners: Priya will own the technical scoping/POC plan; Karthik will lead commercial/contract conversations. I’ll coordinate next meeting invites once we have the econ buyer + procurement contact.

If this looks right, a quick intro reply to this thread with Marco (or whoever owns budget) and procurement would be ideal.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Subject: Re: Brightlane — follow-up and next steps from discovery

Ben — thanks for the clear recap and the ROI template. That’s helpful.

Quick answers:
- Econ buyer / budget owner: Marco Silva, VP Business Operations — marco.silva@brightlanehealth.com. He owns discretionary spend for product/platform pilots this year.
- Procurement: procurement@brightlanehealth.com (I’ve copied them on this reply so they have visibility).
- Budget: we have a pilot budget earmarked in Q3 — ballpark $200–300k depending on model/SLAs; Marco can confirm.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required for production access; for pilot we can discuss scoped access in our VPC.

Looping Marco and procurement in now. Marco — Ben and team from Redwood did a quick discovery with my team yesterday; they build an inference platform we’re evaluating for the triage use case. Would appreciate 20–30 minutes to align on commercial approach and KPIs.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang | Director, Data Platform | Brightlane Health
emily.zhang@brightlanehealth.com

Looping in a few technical notes we should prep before the Marco call:
- Pricing/tiers to have ready: hosted API (pay-as-you-go), committed/dedicated pool (monthly commit), and a pilot pricing tranche with limited tokens and VPC-only data flow.
- Compliance docs: SOC 2 cert + SOC 2 scope summary. Also prepare a short note on data residency and KMS integration options.
- Pilot plan: 6-week pilot, acceptance criteria focused on accuracy of extraction and end-to-end latency under a 400ms p95 target for summary endpoint.

I attached a short pricing one-pager we can adapt for Marco. I recommend we include a simple comparison table (hosted vs dedicated) and a sample MAP milestone list.

Priya

priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Intro + 20-30m to align on outcomes and commercial approach (Brightlane pilot)

Marco — hi, Ben Carter from Redwood Inference here. Emily suggested you’re the right person to align with on budget and commercial approach for a Q3 pilot. Quick context: Redwood runs a production-first inference platform (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC) used by teams that need predictable latency and clear unit economics. For Brightlane we’d propose a scoped pilot to validate integration, clinical extraction accuracy, and a lightweight SLO for latency.

Ask: would you be open to 20–30 minutes next week for a quick alignment conversation? Our agenda would be:
- Confirm high-level outcomes and how Brightlane will measure pilot success (ROI template attached).
- Discuss commercial models (pilot pricing, transition to committed capacity, optional dedicated deployment).
- Procurement/legal next steps and timeline for SOC 2 artifacts and contract review.

I’ve attached a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP-Brightlane-v1.docx) and the ROI template Emily already has. If procurement prefers, we can send the questionnaire separately to procurement@brightlanehealth.com.

Proposed times: Mon 2/23 09:00–12:00 PT or Tue 2/24 13:00–16:00 PT — happy to coordinate a time that works for you.

Thanks — look forward to aligning.

Best,
Ben

ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
